definitions.explanation: The Japanese language and literature from the Heian period through the early modern period. A required subject in Japanese high schools.
Any text written in an older form of a language.

examples.japanese: {古文|こぶん}の{授業|じゅぎょう}は{難|むずか}しい。
{高校|こうこう}で{古文|こぶん}と{漢文|かんぶん}を{習|なら}った。
examples.english: I studied classical Japanese and classical Chinese in high school.

examples.japanese: {古文|こぶん}の{文法|ぶんぽう}は{現代語|げんだいご}とかなり{違|ちが}うので、{慣|な}れるまで{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: Classical Japanese grammar is quite different from modern Japanese, so it takes time to get used to it.

examples.japanese: {古文|こぶん}を{読|よ}み{解|と}く。
{図書館|としょかん}に{貴重|きちょう}な{古文|こぶん}が{保管|ほかん}されている。
examples.english: Valuable ancient texts are stored in the library.

examples.japanese: {専門家|せんもんか}でないと{読|よ}めない{古文|こぶん}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many ancient texts that only specialists can read.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese education, {古文|こぶん} specifically refers to classical Japanese texts (as opposed to {漢文|かんぶん}, classical Chinese texts read in Japanese). Both are required subjects in high school. Students learn to read works like {源氏物語|げんじものがたり} (The Tale of Genji) and {枕草子|まくらのそうし} (The Pillow Book).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {古文|こぶん}の{授業|じゅぎょう} (classical Japanese class)
- {古文|こぶん}{単語|たんご} (classical Japanese vocabulary)
- {古文|こぶん}{文法|ぶんぽう} (classical Japanese grammar)
- {古文|こぶん}を{読|よ}む (to read classical texts)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {漢文|かんぶん}: classical Chinese (read in Japanese) — paired subject in schools
- {古語|こご}: archaic word — refers to individual old words, not texts
